did_you_know.text: Did you know? To repopulate Jerusalem, the people cast lots: one person out of every ten was brought to live in the city, while the other nine settled in the towns.
Did you know? The people blessed those who volunteered to live in Jerusalem, even though they had not been assigned to settle there by lot.
Did you know? The descendants of Judah and Benjamin lived in Jerusalem, including the descendants of Perez and the Shilonites.
Did you know? There were 468 descendants of Perez living in Jerusalem, and they were described as mighty men.
Did you know? The priests living in Jerusalem included Jedaiah, Jakin, and Seraiah; Seraiah was described as the chief officer of the house of God.
Did you know? Mattaniah son of Asaph led the beginning of prayer and thanksgiving, and Bakbukiah served as his assistant.
Did you know? There were 172 gatekeepers serving in Jerusalem, including Akkub and Talmon, who guarded the gates.
Did you know? Not all the other priests and Levites lived in Jerusalem; they lived in the towns of Judah, each on his own inheritance.
Did you know? The singers were given a binding instruction to sing every day, and Uzzi son of Bani was in charge of the Levites and the work of the house of God.

Did you know? The descendants of Benjamin lived in many towns, including Geba, Michmash, Bethel, Anathoth, Ramah, Hadid, Lod, and Ono; at the end of the chapter, divisions of Levites in Judah and Benjamin are also mentioned.
